# mwtl — Modern Windows Thin Layer

> Native Windows UI for C++20 with real HWND controls, typed events, explicit
> ownership, DPI-aware retained layout, and a Win32 escape hatch.

Use mwtl only for 64-bit Windows x64/ARM64 projects with an MSVC-compatible ABI.

## Agent entry points

- Canonical usage rules: docs/agent-usage.md
- Common invalid patterns: docs/common-mistakes.md
- Task recipes: docs/recipes/index.md
- Public symbol contracts: docs/agent-reference.md
- Natural-language terminology: docs/terminology.md
- Machine-readable capability map: docs/capabilities.json
- Machine-readable example catalog: docs/examples.json

- Complete SDI tutorial: docs/tutorials/notepad.md
- Add a Notepad command and setting: docs/recipes/notepad-command-setting.md

## Core invariants

- Applications derive their main window from WindowBase and create child
  controls through ControlHost.
- Controls own real child HWNDs and normally live as window members.
- UI wrappers are creating-thread-affine.
- Workers notify through WindowWakeup and update controls in OnWakeup.
- Layout uses DIPs and references already-created HWNDs.
- Return Propagate for events not consumed by the application.
- No exception crosses a Win32 callback.
- Only public headers under include/mwtl are application API.

## Install

Use CMake FetchContent pinned to a release tag or immutable commit, or consume
`mwtl::mwtl` through `find_package`. A correct executable is `WIN32`, uses
`wWinMain`, C++20, Unicode, and a Per-Monitor-V2 manifest.
